neighbours.label: in clinical text, the part or degree word just before 'affected' or 'involved' (which nerves, muscles or limbs a disease reaches, or how severely)
fire: In this form of polyneuropathy the legs are often more severely affected.
Symptoms differ according to the cranial nerves affected and can include double vision.
Ptosis appears when the muscles innervated by the third nerve are affected.
In some patients the motor fibers are more markedly affected than sensory ones.
Depending on the spinal roots involved, weakness may appear in either arm.
A child may have several joints affected at the onset of arthritis.
Older dogs may have all four limbs severely affected by the disease.
Severity depends on which nerve is affected and how long the pressure lasts.
quiet: In this form of polyneuropathy the treatment is often long and costly.
Prescriptions differ according to the insurance plan and can include generics.
Ptosis surgery takes about an hour and is usually done in a clinic.
In some patients the dose is lowered after the first month.
Depending on the test results, treatment may begin next week.
A child may need several vaccines at the first visit.
Older dogs may need a softer diet and a shorter walk.
Recovery depends on age and on how long the patient rests.

short: before 'affected': which body part, how severely
notes: The card's top examples also include non-medical peaks (' were', 'Ne'), so this probably covers only part of the pole.
